title: Rest in Christ
definition: Rest in Christ is the believer's trustful relief from striving, condemnation, anxiety, and self-salvation through the finished work and gentle care of Jesus.
summary: Rest in Christ is the soul's ceasing from self-salvation, anxious striving, and burdensome self-rule by trusting Jesus.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is gentle and lowly in heart, giving rest to those burdened by sin and weakness.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on Gospel rest. Christ gives rest to weary sinners who cannot carry guilt, law-keeping, fear, or control. Rest does not mean laziness; it means laboring from acceptance in Christ rather than for acceptance.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because many believers are exhausted by trying to prove, fix, control, or justify themselves. Rest in Christ brings the heart back to His finished work and gentle lordship. It is especially precious for the burdened, disabled, recovering, and weary.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Name the burdens you are carrying as though Christ had not finished His work. Come to Him in prayer with honest weariness. Practice obedience from rest, not panic.
